chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qarashi reported to me with a permission to transmit, that Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal reported from al-Husayn ibn Nasr, who reported from his father, who reported from Abdul Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, who reported from al-Minhal ibn Amr who said he heard Abul Qasim Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hanafiyya (may Allah be pleased with him) saying:

"There is nothing for you in your life except a pleasure that draws you nearer to your death and brings you closer to your sleep. What food is there that is not accompanied by choking? Or what drink that is not accompanied by strangling?

So ponder over your affairs, for it is as if you have already become the lost beloved and the phantom carried away. The people of this world are people on a journey; they do not unpack their baggage except in another place."

key_terms.المخترم: Al-Mukhtaram: snatched away, carried off (by death)
key_terms.شرق: Sharaq: choking on liquid, strangling while drinking
key_terms.غصص: Ghusas: choking, lumps in the throat (metaphor for hidden suffering)

ai.seo_question: What did Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya say about worldly pleasures and the transience of life?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, the son of Imam Ali (AS), delivers a powerful admonition about the deceptive nature of worldly pleasures. Speaking to the early Muslim community in Medina and Kufa during the turbulent post-Karbala era, he warns that every worldly pleasure only brings one closer to death. The metaphor of travelers who never unpack their luggage except at their final destination encapsulates the Islamic teaching that this world is merely a temporary passage to the hereafter.
